VGK.head: Leaning the Golden Knights’ way
VGK.body: Even though Vegas will be without Hanifin and Dallas gets Heiskanen back, the Golden Knights have home-ice advantage and have been out-chancing opponents lately. Still, it’s close: the Stars can make it interesting if they keep shots to a minimum.

story.head: Two good teams
paras: The Golden Knights (13-6-3) lost 6-3 to Vancouver on Sunday, while the Stars have won two in a row. Two good teams meet. Going in, the Stars are fourth in the Central (14th in the NHL) and the Knights second in the Pacific (fifth).
This season, the Golden Knights have outscored teams 73-61, but only 44-42 at 5-on-5. On special teams, they’ve outscored teams 23-16.

The Stars block more shots than anyone (1st) and have a dangerous power play (1st). Dallas has allowed 2.40 goals a game, the third fewest in the league. As for the Golden Knights, they draw more penalties than they take (1st) and create more chances on the penalty kill than almost anyone (2nd). They also have the league’s best penalty kill (1st), and the Stars’ power play against their penalty killers is strength against strength. Both teams play slow, low-event hockey, especially the Stars (lowest), so expect a tight one.

Jason Robertson (10 G / 12 A / 22 P in 20 GP) is tied for the Stars’ scoring lead. Mikko Rantanen (9 G / 13 A / 22 P in 20 GP) shares it, with four goals in six games against Vegas since 2023-24. For the Golden Knights, Jack Eichel (9 G / 18 A / 27 P in 22 GP) leads the way in scoring, with six goals in nine games against Dallas since 2023-24. Mark Stone (11 G / 10 A / 21 P in 22 GP) has a team-high eleven goals.
Jake Oettinger (10-4-1 / .902 SV% in 15 GS) is expected to start for Dallas, and Adin Hill (7-2-1 / .907 SV% in 10 GS) for Vegas.
